warnings.message: Prefixes are the exact addresses observed. Cloud and CDN services change addresses; prefer DNS names where the destination is a named service, and review whether DNS resolution should be allowed (the Allow all DNS queries setting is left off).
Observed services are for reference. Egress policies can name services, whose definition depends on the platform.

review_items.message: These proposals come only from the capture window described under Observation. Dependencies that did not occur in that window are invisible to this tool: scheduled or seasonal jobs, backup and failover paths, maintenance and vendor access, start-up sequences, rarely used engineering functions, and anything outside the observation point. Confirm each proposal with the people who run the systems before enforcing it.

10.30.2.40 and 10.20.1.60 (udp 514): which side initiates is uncertain (low confidence: only datagrams from 10.30.2.40:514 were seen). No policy was proposed. Decide the direction before creating one; a wrong direction would permit the opposite initiation.
initiator 2001:db8:20::15 and responder 2001:db8:30::40 are not in any group, so the communication was not turned into a policy. Add the address to a group.

Absence from this capture is not evidence of absence: devices, subnets, ports and protocols that never appear may simply not have been visible to the capture point or active during this period.

facts.name: Directional group policy model
defined: A policy connects one or more From groups to one or more To groups.
From groups may initiate connections to To groups within the policy; To groups may not initiate to From groups.
Direction is about who may initiate a connection. Replies to a permitted connection are not a separate permission.
Allowing both directions needs two policies.
An endpoint can belong to several groups and a group can appear in several policies.

An external egress policy is a separate type for endpoints isolated behind a gateway. It names the endpoint groups, the allowed external destinations (address prefixes and DNS names, optionally recursive), optional services, whether all DNS queries are allowed, and whether the policy is enabled.
not_modelled: Ports and protocols as enforced conditions on a group policy (kept only as information).
Deny actions, and rule ordering or precedence.
How a named service for an egress policy is defined on a particular platform.
facts.note: This is a model defined by this application so that policies can be reviewed in one neutral form. It is not the policy format of any product. Check what your enforcement platform supports before relying on any row.

manual_steps: Create each group listed in the Groups table on your enforcement platform and add its endpoints (group membership is not imported from this worksheet).
For each row of the Group policies table, create one policy from the From groups to the To groups. Create one policy per direction; a policy never grants the reverse direction.
For each row of the Egress policies table, create an external egress policy for the endpoint groups with the allowed prefixes and DNS names, and decide on services and DNS handling yourself.

Services (ports/protocols) in the worksheet are for reference. The directional model does not enforce them; if your platform can, apply them there, otherwise accept that the policy is broader than the source.
Review every item under Review and Gaps before enabling anything. This worksheet is not proof that the result is equivalent to the source; it is a starting point.
